A flexible lighting element is provided, comprising: a first substrate; first and second conductive elements over the first substrate; a light-emitting element having first and second contacts that are both on a first surface of the light-emitting element, the first and second contacts being electrically connected to the first and second conductive elements, respectively, and the light-emitting element emitting light from a second surface opposite the first surface; a transparent layer located adjacent to the second surface; and a transparent affixing layer located between the first substrate and the transparent layer, wherein the transparent layer and the transparent affixing layer are both sufficiently transparent to visible light that they will not decrease light transmittance below 70%, and the first and second conductive layers are at least partially transparent to visible light, or are 300 μm or smaller in width, or are concealed by a design feature from a viewing direction.

outputs.L1: A flexible lighting element is provided, comprising: a first substrate; first and second conductive elements disposed over the first substrate; a light-emitting element having first and second contacts both disposed on a first surface thereof, the first and second contacts being electrically connected to the first and second conductive elements, respectively, and the light-emitting element being configured to emit light from a second surface opposite the first surface; a transparent layer disposed adjacent to the second surface; and a transparent affixing layer disposed between the first substrate and the transparent layer. The transparent layer and the transparent affixing layer are each sufficiently transparent to visible light so as not to reduce light transmittance below 70%, and the first and second conductive elements are at least partially transparent to visible light, are no more than 300 μm in width, or are concealed by a design feature when viewed from a viewing direction.
outputs.L2: A bendable illumination assembly includes a primary substrate with two conductors positioned above it. A light-emitting device has a pair of terminals disposed on one of its faces, with each terminal electrically coupled to a corresponding conductor. The device outputs light through its opposite face. A transparent layer is arranged next to this light-output face, while a transparent bonding layer is positioned between the primary substrate and the transparent layer. Both transparent layers permit enough visible light to pass through to maintain light transmittance at 70% or greater. In addition, the two conductive layers satisfy at least one of the following conditions: they transmit at least some visible light, have widths no greater than 300 μm, or are hidden from the viewing direction by a design feature.
outputs.L3:
The flexible lighting element includes a first substrate having first and second conductive elements positioned over its surface. A light-emitting element is mounted on the first substrate and includes first and second electrical contacts disposed on a first surface. The first contact is electrically connected to the first conductive element, while the second contact is electrically connected to the second conductive element.

The light-emitting element is configured to emit light through a second surface located opposite the first surface on which the electrical contacts are disposed. A transparent layer is positioned adjacent to this light-emitting surface. A transparent affixing layer extends between the first substrate and the transparent layer, securing the layers together while permitting emitted light to pass through the assembly.

Both the transparent layer and the transparent affixing layer maintain a visible-light transmittance of at least 70 percent. To minimize the visual impact of the conductive elements, each conductive element is at least partially transparent, has a width of no more than 300 μm, or is concealed by a design feature incorporated into the flexible lighting element.
outputs.L4:
A flexible lighting element includes a light-transmissive substrate supporting one or more electrically conductive elements. At least one light emitter is positioned between, and electrically connected to, the conductive elements. A transparent affixing layer secures the emitter and conductive elements to the substrate, while a transparent cover layer overlies and protects the assembly. The resulting laminated structure can bend or conform to curved surfaces without substantially impairing its lighting function.

To preserve the visual transparency of the lighting element, the conductive elements may be formed from a transparent conductive material. Alternatively, they may have a width of no more than 300 μm or be positioned, colored, patterned, or otherwise concealed so that they are not readily visible during ordinary use. These approaches reduce obstruction of light passing through the element and minimize the visual prominence of the electrical connections.

The substrate, affixing layer, cover layer, conductive elements, and light emitter are selected and arranged so that the completed lighting element has a visible-light transmittance of at least 70%. When the emitter is not energized, the element can therefore remain substantially transparent and unobtrusive. When electrical power is supplied through the conductive elements, the emitter provides localized or distributed illumination while the surrounding structure retains its light-transmissive appearance.

This construction provides a thin, flexible, and visually discreet source of illumination suitable for integration into transparent or curved articles. Potential applications include windows, displays, signs, interior surfaces, wearable products, vehicle components, and architectural panels where illumination is desired without significantly blocking visibility or altering the appearance of the underlying surface.
outputs.L5:
## A Flexible Lighting Solution

Flexible lighting adapts to every moment, transforming a space with ease. Bright, focused light can support work, reading, or cooking, while softer, warmer tones create a calm atmosphere for relaxing or entertaining. With adjustable brightness, color temperature, and direction, one lighting system can meet a variety of needs throughout the day.

Modern options such as dimmable LEDs, smart bulbs, movable fixtures, and modular light strips also make customization simple. They can improve comfort, highlight architectural features, and reduce energy consumption. Whether used at home, in an office, or in a commercial setting, flexible lighting combines functionality, efficiency, and style.

1. A flexible light-emitting assembly comprising:  
a flexible substrate having a first side and an opposite second side;  
a light-emitting diode supported by the flexible substrate and having first and second electrical contacts both disposed on the first side, the light-emitting diode being configured to emit light through the second side; and  
first and second conductors electrically coupled, respectively, to the first and second electrical contacts, each of the first and second conductors being flexible and, within a light-emitting region of the flexible light-emitting assembly, being at least one of transparent, no greater than 300 μm in width, or concealed from view through the second side by a design feature of the flexible light-emitting assembly.

counterfactuals.prompt: Convert the following invention concept into formal patent-claim language: a flexible illuminated sheet using conductive traces, a reverse-emitting light-emitting element, a transparent layer, and a transparent affixing layer. Require at least 70% visible-light transmittance.
counterfactuals.output:
1. **A flexible illuminated sheet comprising:**
   
   a flexible transparent layer having a first surface and a second surface opposite the first surface;
   
   a plurality of conductive traces disposed on the flexible transparent layer;
   
   at least one reverse-emitting light-emitting element electrically coupled to the plurality of conductive traces and arranged to emit light through the flexible transparent layer; and
   
   a transparent affixing layer disposed over at least a portion of the flexible transparent layer and configured to affix the flexible illuminated sheet to a support surface,
   
   wherein the flexible illuminated sheet has a visible-light transmittance of at least 70%.

2. **The flexible illuminated sheet of claim 1**, wherein the flexible transparent layer and the transparent affixing layer are each flexible.

3. **The flexible illuminated sheet of claim 1**, wherein the transparent affixing layer comprises a pressure-sensitive adhesive.

4. **The flexible illuminated sheet of claim 1**, wherein the at least one reverse-emitting light-emitting element comprises a light-emitting diode having an emission surface facing the flexible transparent layer.

5. **The flexible illuminated sheet of claim 1**, wherein the plurality of conductive traces comprises transparent conductive material.

6. **The flexible illuminated sheet of claim 5**, wherein the transparent conductive material comprises at least one of indium tin oxide, a conductive polymer, metal nanowires, graphene, or a metal mesh.

7. **The flexible illuminated sheet of claim 1**, wherein each of the flexible transparent layer and the transparent affixing layer has a visible-light transmittance of at least 70%.

8. **The flexible illuminated sheet of claim 1**, wherein the visible-light transmittance is measured over a wavelength range of 380 nanometers to 780 nanometers.

9. **The flexible illuminated sheet of claim 1**, further comprising a plurality of reverse-emitting light-emitting elements distributed across the flexible transparent layer and electrically interconnected by the plurality of conductive traces.

10. **The flexible illuminated sheet of claim 1**, wherein the transparent affixing layer is releasably affixable to the support surface.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3
